design_philosophy: Inspired by Tinder's swipe simplicity and Discord's immersive dark atmosphere. Designed for gamers, highlighting deep blacks with intentional neon blue and purple accents to create a premium, night-time gaming feel.

swipe_card.style: Full-height image taking up 70-80% of the screen. Absolute positioning.
swipe_card.overlay: LinearGradient from transparent to rgba(5,5,5,0.95) at the bottom 40% to ensure text readability.

bottom_navigation.background: Dark translucent view with BlurView equivalent style

interactions_and_animations.swipe_gestures: Use react-native-reanimated for smooth 60fps Tinder-like swiping. Map X-translation to rotation (max 15deg at screen edge).
interactions_and_animations.swipe_overlays: As card moves right, fade in 'LIKE' neon badge. As card moves left, fade in 'PASS' badge.
interactions_and_animations.button_press: Scale down to 0.95 on press-in, scale back to 1 on press-out using React Native Animated or Reanimated.

instructions_to_main_agent: Build standard React Native Expo app files. Use standard React Native StyleSheet unless NativeWind is pre-configured.
For the Tinder swipe card, use react-native-reanimated and react-native-gesture-handler. Do not use outdated swipe deck libraries.
Ensure all backgrounds use the #050505 deep black. Avoid standard #000000 to maintain depth.
Implement the linear gradient overlay on the swipe card using expo-linear-gradient to ensure text readability over the image.
Always use lucide-react-native for icons. Specifically, use icons like Gamepad2, Sparkles, MessageSquare, User, Flame.
Add 'data-testid' to all touchables, buttons, and form inputs for robust automated testing.
Since the user specified 'iOS-first', use standard iOS Safe Area insets (SafeAreaView) and smooth spring animations.
Do not use HTML tags like <div> or <span>; this is React Native (<View>, <Text>, <TouchableOpacity>, <Image>).
